Table MY-1 lists Treasury market bid yields at constant maturities for bills, notes, and bonds. The Treasury yield curve in the accompanying chart is based on current market bid quotations on the most actively traded Treasury securities as of 3:30 p.m. on the last business day of the calendar quarter. The Treasury uses quotations obtained by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to derive the yield curve, based on semiannual interest payments and read at constant maturity points to develop a consistent data series. The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System publishes the Treasury constant maturity data series in its weekly Statistical Release H.15. On July 31, 2001, Treasury expanded its constant maturity index to include a 1-month constant maturity yield, and Table MY-1 now includes a 1-month maturity beginning on that date. On February 18, 2002, Treasury discontinued the 30-year constant maturity yield. In lieu of the 30-year yield, Table MY-1 will include a 20-year maturity. Historical data for the 20-year maturity is available from the Board of Governors' Statistical Release H.15. Prior to January 2003, this section also included data on long-term Treasury, corporate and municipal yields (Table MY-2). python3 << 'EOF'
# 10-year constant maturity nominal yields (monthly averages) from the data

# 1993 data
data_1993 = {
    'Jan': 6.60, 'Feb': 6.26, 'Mar': 5.98, 'Apr': 5.97, 'May': 6.04,
    'Jun': 5.96, 'Jul': 5.81, 'Aug': 5.68, 'Sep': 5.36, 'Oct': 5.33,
    'Nov': 5.72, 'Dec': 5.77
}

# 1998 data
data_1998 = {
    'Jan': 5.54, 'Feb': 5.57, 'Mar': 5.65, 'Apr': 5.64, 'May': 5.65,
    'Jun': 5.50, 'Jul': 5.46, 'Aug': 5.34, 'Sep': 4.81, 'Oct': 4.53,
    'Nov': 4.83, 'Dec': 4.65
}

# 2003 data
data_2003 = {
    'Jan': 4.05, 'Feb': 3.90, 'Mar': 3.81, 'Apr': 3.96, 'May': 3.57,
    'Jun': 3.33, 'Jul': 3.98, 'Aug': 4.45, 'Sep': 4.27, 'Oct': 4.29,
    'Nov': 4.30, 'Dec': 4.27
}

# Ordered months
months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']

# Calculate 3-month moving averages for March through December
# March 3-month avg = (Jan + Feb + Mar) / 3
# April 3-month avg = (Feb + Mar + Apr) / 3
# etc.

all_moving_averages = []

for year_name, data in [('1993', data_1993), ('1998', data_1998), ('2003', data_2003)]:
    print(f"\n=== {year_name} ===")
    # For March to December (indices 2 to 11)
    for i in range(2, 12):  # March (index 2) to December (index 11)
        # The 3-month period ends in the current month
        m1, m2, m3 = months[i-2], months[i-1], months[i]
        avg = (data[m1] + data[m2] + data[m3]) / 3
        print(f"{m3}: ({data[m1]:.2f} + {data[m2]:.2f} + {data[m3]:.2f}) / 3 = {avg:.4f}")
        all_moving_averages.append(avg)

print("\n=== ALL MOVING AVERAGES ===")
print(all_moving_averages)

print(f"\n=== RANGE CALCULATION ===")
min_ma = min(all_moving_averages)
max_ma = max(all_moving_averages)
range_val = max_ma - min_ma
print(f"Min: {min_ma:.4f}")
print(f"Max: {max_ma:.4f}")
print(f"Range (max - min): {range_val:.4f}")
print(f"Rounded to nearest hundredths: {round(range_val, 2)}")
EOF
